classification.difficultyReason: Applies the quotient rule and exact inverse trigonometric values to establish a specified gradient.

content.prompt: Show that the gradient of the curve $y=\dfrac{\sin^{-1}x}{x}$ at the point where $x=\dfrac12$ is $\dfrac23(2\sqrt3-\pi)$.

answer.worked:
By the quotient rule,
$$\begin{aligned}\frac{dy}{dx}&=\frac{\dfrac{x}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}-\sin^{-1}x}{x^2}.\end{aligned}$$
At $x=\dfrac12$, $\sin^{-1}\!\left(\dfrac12\right)=\dfrac\pi6$ and $\sqrt{1-\dfrac14}=\dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}$.
$$\begin{aligned}\left.\frac{dy}{dx}\right|_{x=1/2}&=\frac{\dfrac{1/2}{\sqrt3/2}-\pi/6}{1/4}\\&=4\left(\frac1{\sqrt3}-\frac\pi6\right)\\&=\frac4{\sqrt3}-\frac{2\pi}{3}\\&=\frac{4\sqrt3}{3}-\frac{2\pi}{3}\\&=\frac23(2\sqrt3-\pi).\end{aligned}$$
